title: Update PRD: runtime degradation mitigations, automated fallbacks, and acceptance tests driven by KV-cache incident
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Translate decisions and action items from the December KV-cache incident postmortem into concrete PRD changes. Goal is to reduce customer-visible degradation in tail-latency and error rates when cache misses or compaction events occur. The PRD updates must specify new SLO tolerances, required automated fallback behavior, rollout constraints, and explicit acceptance tests (synthetic and integration) that will gate release. This ticket coordinates PM requirements, eng implementation scope, and console/observability requirements so that the engineering work has clear acceptance criteria and owners.

Background: During the KV-cache incident, an infrequent cache compaction path caused large numbers of cold requests to bypass optimized execution and hit a slower kernel path. This produced a latency spike that breached the P99 latency SLO for several customers. The postmortem proposed short-term mitigations (prefix warmup, stricter batch-size limits) and longer-term runtime changes (compaction staged background eviction, health-aware routing). This PRD update must capture both immediate acceptance gates and long-term requirements for Dedicated and Hosted runtimes.

Scope: PRD must include: SLO changes and measurement windows, deterministic fallback policy for cache-affected requests, canary and rollback criteria, required telemetry and traces, synthetic warmup tests, and post-release monitoring dashboards. Exclusions: kernel implementation details will be designed by Eng and captured in ENG tickets; this PRD focuses on observable behavior and acceptance conditions by product and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: SLOs: Define explicit P95/P99 latency SLOs and error-rate thresholds for both steady-state and cache-compaction windows; SLOs must include a separate 'compaction-burst' window with tolerances and recovery targets.

Automated fallback: Runtime must support a policy that routes requests to a compatible model variant or lower-latency path when cache-miss rate > 2% sustained for 60s. Fallback must be transparent to client with structured reason codes emitted to traces.

Canary: New runtime changes are gated by a two-stage canary: 1) internal synthetic traffic (10k requests/hour) for 24h with no P99 regression >10%; 2) customer-visible canary on <=5% of traffic with automatic rollback if error-rate increases >1% absolute or P99 increase >20%.

Observability: Dashboard showing cache miss rate, compaction triggers, P50/P95/P99 latencies, errors, fallback activations, and request distribution by variant. Dashboard panels and alert rules must be specified in the PRD and linked to runbooks.
Synthetic acceptance tests: End-to-end runbook that reproduces compaction-like cold starts using the same request distributions; test must run in staging and pass before canary promotion.

Runbook & playbooks: Include specific runbook steps for detecting and mitigating compaction-driven spikes (alert thresholds, mitigation steps: throttle, fallback activate, scale-up, rollback), with clear owner (SRE on-call) and escalation paths.

Security & data: Any fallback path must maintain customer data isolation guarantees (no cross-customer KV reuse); PRD must require a security review if fallback interacts with private deployment configs.

Release gating: All above items must be validated in staging and during canary before marking release as Done in the PRD. A post-deploy check-in (72h) is required to confirm recovery metrics and to sign off.
Documentation: Update Console docs and API changelog to include new fallback semantics and structured reason codes.
Compatibility: Dedicated and Private deployments must have optional opt-in toggles for experimental fallback behavior; default behavior in Hosted must align with PRD.
Testing: Include both unit/integration tests (ENG) and black-box acceptance tests (PM/SRE) with exact pass/fail criteria documented in PRD.
Stakeholder signoff: PM, Eng lead, SRE lead, and Product Security must explicitly sign-off on PRD acceptance criteria prior to schedule freeze.
notes_and_decisions: 2025-01-13 - Asha: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Jingwei Chen), SRE (Lucas Meyer), and Console (Rina Das). Agreed scope: PRD to require explicit structured reason codes for fallbacks. Action: ENG to sketch fallback API contract.
2025-01-15 - Miguel: Reviewed Eng prototype for fallback routing. Decision: initial threshold set to 2% sustained cache-miss over 60s; Eng to validate in staging and propose telemetry tags.
2025-01-16 - Rina: Console team will add a dashboard template; PM to include required panels. Follow-up: link dashboard prototype in artifacts once available.
2025-01-17 - Security (Anika Rao): Confirmed that fallback path design must be auditable; requested security_review_required flag in PRD. Deferred deep crypto review to ENG implementation.
2025-01-18 - Miguel: Added canary thresholds and rollback criteria. Agreed to require automated rollback triggers that can be disabled per-customer in Dedicated/Private via config.
2025-01-19 - PM review: Incorporated feedback that synthetic warmup tests should use real-world request mixes and token length distributions; SRE to author test harness.
2025-01-20 - Decision: Release target set to runtime-2025.03; staging validation window = 48h; post-deploy signoff at 72h. Action owners assigned and ENG tickets created.
final_notes: This PRD update is driven by incident learnings and must be treated as high priority. The PRD focuses on observable behavior and acceptance gates; implementation details will live in dependent ENG tickets. After canary, schedule a retrospective to assess whether acceptance criteria were sufficient and update PRD accordingly.
